name: Hospital Bag / Duffel
description: A roomy bag that's easy to grab on the way out the door — pack it by week 36.

name: ID, Insurance Card & Hospital Paperwork
description: Photo ID, insurance card, pre-registration forms, and your birth plan if you have one.

name: Phone Charger (long cord)
description: Hospital outlets are rarely near the bed — a long cord or a short extension cable helps.

name: Going-Home Outfit (for you)
description: Something loose and comfortable — you'll still look several months pregnant right after birth.

name: Nursing Bra or Soft Bralette
description: Wire-free and easy to nurse in, even if you're not sure yet whether you'll breastfeed.

name: Maternity or High-Waisted Underwear
description: Many hospitals provide mesh underwear, but bringing your own for the ride home is worth it.

name: Toiletries Bag
description: Toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant, hairbrush, hair ties, lip balm — the basics for a multi-day stay.

name: Flip-Flops or Slides for the Shower
description: Hospital shower floors aren't somewhere you want bare feet.

name: Robe or Comfortable Cover-Up
description: For walking the halls during early labor or postpartum recovery without feeling exposed.

name: Your Own Pillow
description: Hospital pillows are thin — a pillow from home (with a distinct pillowcase so it doesn't get lost) is a comfort upgrade.

name: Snacks
description: Labor can be long, and hospital food service hours are limited. Easy, non-messy snacks help.

name: Lip Balm & Hair Ties
description: Small comfort items that are easy to forget and genuinely useful during labor.

name: Going-Home Outfit (for baby)
description: Weather-appropriate, newborn or 0-3 month size — babies vary a lot in birth weight.

name: Rear-Facing Infant Car Seat
description: Most hospitals will not discharge a newborn without a properly installed car seat — install it before your due date, not after.

name: Swaddle Blanket
description: Hospitals provide swaddle blankets, but bringing your own for the ride home is common.

name: Newborn Hat
description: Newborns lose heat quickly through their heads — hospitals usually provide one, but a soft one from home is a nice touch for photos.

name: Change of Clothes & Toiletries (partner/support person)
description: Labor and hospital stays run long — pack for at least an overnight stay.

name: Phone Charger & Entertainment
description: There can be long stretches of waiting — a book, headphones, or a downloaded show helps.

name: Cash & Snacks for Vending Machines
description: Not every hospital cafeteria takes card, and hours are limited overnight.

name: Pillow & Blanket
description: Most hospital rooms have a fold-out chair or cot for a support person, but not always bedding.

name: Postpartum Recovery Underwear
description: High-waisted, breathable, and disposable-friendly — you'll go through several pairs a day at first.

name: Nipple Cream
description: Useful from day one if you're planning to breastfeed.

name: Comfortable Nursing-Friendly Pajamas
description: Button-front or wrap-style tops make nursing and skin-to-skin easier during your stay.
